"""Standalone verification of the #15022-style admin search join fix.

Avoids django.test (which imports asgiref) by configuring settings manually
and using ModelAdmin.get_search_results() directly.
"""
import sys
sys.path.insert(0, "C:/Users/agent/work/work/django-15022-nopanel")

import django
from django.conf import settings

settings.configure(
    DEBUG=True,
    DATABASES={"default": {"ENGINE": "django.db.backends.sqlite3", "NAME": ":memory:"}},
    INSTALLED_APPS=[
        "django.contrib.contenttypes",
        "django.contrib.auth",
        "django.contrib.admin",
        "django.contrib.sessions",
        "django.contrib.messages",
    ],
    ROOT_URLCONF=None,
    USE_TZ=True,
    DEFAULT_AUTO_FIELD="django.db.models.AutoField",
)
django.setup()

from django.db import models, connection
from django.contrib import admin


class Client(models.Model):
    name = models.CharField(max_length=256)
    name2 = models.CharField(max_length=256, blank=True, null=True)
    contact_person = models.CharField(max_length=256, blank=True, null=True)

    class Meta:
        app_label = "verify"


class ClientOffice(models.Model):
    name = models.CharField(max_length=256)
    name2 = models.CharField(max_length=256, blank=True, null=True)
    client = models.ForeignKey(Client, on_delete=models.CASCADE)

    class Meta:
        app_label = "verify"


class ClientAdmin(admin.ModelAdmin):
    search_fields = ("name", "name2", "contact_person", "clientoffice__name", "clientoffice__name2")


with connection.schema_editor() as se:
    se.create_model(Client)
    se.create_model(ClientOffice)

# Data: client 1 matches all three words across its office rows;
# client 2 matches only one word.
c1 = Client.objects.create(name="foo bar baz corp", name2="acme", contact_person="john")
ClientOffice.objects.create(name="foo branch", name2="bar desk", client=c1)
ClientOffice.objects.create(name="baz office", name2="qux", client=c1)
c2 = Client.objects.create(name="unrelated corp", name2="foo", contact_person="x")
ClientOffice.objects.create(name="foo only", name2="nothing", client=c2)

ma = ClientAdmin(Client, admin.site)

# --- 1. Join count: multi-word search must not add one JOIN per word ---
from django.db import reset_queries
reset_queries()
qs, may_dup = ma.get_search_results(None, Client.objects.all(), "foo bar baz")
sql = str(qs.query)
n_joins = sql.upper().count(" JOIN ")
print("SQL:", sql)
print("JOIN count for 3-word search:", n_joins)

# --- 2. Semantics preserved: terms are ANDed, fields ORed ---
results = set(qs)
print("results for 'foo bar baz':", [r.name for r in results])
assert results == {c1}, "multi-word search should return only client 1"

qs2, _ = ma.get_search_results(None, Client.objects.all(), "foo")
results2 = set(qs2)
print("results for 'foo':", sorted(r.name for r in results2))
assert results2 == {c1, c2}, "single-word search should return both clients"

# quoted phrase still works
qs3, _ = ma.get_search_results(None, Client.objects.all(), '"bar baz"')
assert set(qs3) == {c1}, "quoted phrase search broken"

# --- 3. Single-word search: identical SQL shape as before (one JOIN) ---
reset_queries()
qs4, _ = ma.get_search_results(None, Client.objects.all(), "foo")
sql4 = str(qs4.query)
print("JOIN count for 1-word search:", sql4.upper().count(" JOIN "))

print()
print("may_have_duplicates:", may_dup)
print("ALL CHECKS PASSED")
